entry.dc:title: Development of methods to improve performance of surface mine sediment basins
entry.dc:creator: Ettinger C.E.
entry.dc:description: Because of the hydrologic conditions and steep terrain in Appalachia, a large share of the eroded material comes from surface mines, largely controlled through the use of sedimentation ponds. Environmental Protection Agency has mandated that sediment basins be designed to achieve a specific effluent quality. Two methods for achieving this goal have been investigated: physical modifications to sediment basin design parameters and the use of chemical coagulants. Methods have been determined for upgrading sediment pond efficencies by physical modifications and coagulant usage. -from US Govt Reports Announcements, 22, 1980

entry.dc:title: Establishment of bryophytes on a reclained surface mine site at Goose Lake Prairie State Park, Illinois.
entry.dc:creator: Rastorfer J.
entry.dc:description: Thirty moss species and one liverwort species were identified from the site, and 2 additional moss species were found in areas adjacent to the site. Bryophytes should help reduce soil erosion by binding soil particles via their rhizoidal systems, and by the relatively high water-holding capacity of their gametophytic shoots; bryophytes might reduce heavy-metal toxicity to certain vascular plants at soil surfaces, because they have an ability to accumulate these elements; and bryophytes may enhance N-fixation through their associations with blue-green algae and possibly with N/fixing bacteria. -from US Govt Reports Announcements, 24, 1981

entry.dc:title: STRUCTURE RESPONSE AND DAMAGE PRODUCED BY GROUND VIBRATION FROM SURFACE MINE BLASTING.
entry.dc:creator: Siskind D.E.
entry.prism:publicationName: Report of Investigations United States Bureau of Mines
entry.dc:description: The Bureau of Mines studied blast-produced ground vibration to assess its damage and annoyance potential, and to determine safe levels and appropriate measurement techniques. Direct measurements were made of ground-vibration-produced structure responses and damage in 76 homes for 219 production blasts. These results were combined with damage data from nine other blasting studies, including the three analyzed previously for Bureau of Mines Bulletin 656.

entry.dc:title: Implementation of US Surface Mine and Reclamation Act
entry.dc:creator: Sani E.
entry.dc:description: The US Congress is currently studying various ways through which legislation similar to that of the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977— which is concerned mainly with coal, can be applied to all minerals other than coal. This study analyses three US mineral industries—copper, iron ore, and phosphate rock - and identifies a number of areas which Congress and other decision makers ought to consider in arriving at such legislation. The author concludes that reclamation costs may affect the economic and financial performance of each of these industries in a different manner; furthermore, their economic behaviour is significantly different from that of coal. The author's main recommendation is that if surface mining regulations are to be legislated, they should be industry- and commodity-specific rather than umbrella legislation for all non-coal minerals. © 1980, All rights reserved.

entry.dc:description: The basic idea behind mountain top removal is that 100 percent of the coal is recovered. Amherst Coal Co. operates one such mountain top removal surface mine in areas of Logan and Wyoming counties near Lundale, W. Va.

entry.dc:title: AMHERST MOUNTAINTOP MINING KEEPS ON TRUCKIN'.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Amherst Coal Company's Lundale 3-A surface mine in southern West Virginia moves over 90 million cu yd of overburden each year with truck and shovel, mountaintop removal mining. Amherst gives priority attention to truck availability and efficiency to keep the mine operating profitably. Presently the Logan County operation has four Dart Model 3100 end dump trucks that have averaged about 96% availability. The payload rating is 100 tons. In addition Amherst operates 13 Euclid end dumps - two 35-ton, one 50-ton and ten 105-ton.

entry.dc:title: A design model for sediment control on mined lands.
entry.dc:creator: Barfield B.
entry.prism:publicationName: In Symp on Watershed Management 1980 Boise U S A Jul 21 23 1980
entry.prism:volume: 2 , New York, U.S.A., Am. Soc. Civ. Engrs., 1980, Session D1, p.628-642. (ISBN 0-87262-250-9)
entry.dc:description: A simple approach to surface mine sedimentology is presented in which the watershed is subdivided into homogeneous subwatersheds and flow and sediment routed to a reservoir. Flow calculations are made using SCS procedures and sediment yields using Williams' routing procedures. Size distribution of the sediment entering the reservoir is calculated using procedures which assume that the large particles are trapped first. Reservoir sedimentology is predicted in the model by using the DEPOSITS routines which predict outflow concentrations and size distributions from continuity principles and plug flow concept. (from authors' abstract)

entry.dc:title: Area strip mine reclamation using dredged material: a field demonstration'
entry.dc:creator: Perrier E.
entry.dc:description: This report describes the application of dredged material for area strip mine reclamation as a possible alternative to the present practices of dredged material disposalY The purpose of the study was to demonstrate the feasibility of using a cover of dewatered dredged material to reclaim surface mine spoils. The goal of the reclamation effort was the prevention and abatement of erosion and acid mine drainage by the use of dredged material as a media for a vegetative cover. (from authors abstract)

entry.dc:title: All-hydraulic surface miner cuts coal with 128,000 ft.-lb. of torque.
entry.dc:creator: Rink R.
entry.dc:description: A 100-ton, all-hydraulic, continuous surface mine, cuts, sizes, and loads up to 2800 tons of lignite or bituminous coal per hour. A 7-ft. diam. cutting head cuts the coal, like a planer, taking out a 12.8ft.-wide bite, to a maximum depth of 2 ft. THe hydraulic controls permit cuts of precise depths to allow cuats within inches of seam bottoms. Four low-speed, high-torque (LSHT) hydraulic motors, which develop 64,000 ft.-lb. torque, drive the cutting head. The head feeds loosened coal from each end toward the center and onto hydraulically drive conveyors for loading into hauler trucks. A detailed account and rationalisation of the design of the hydraulic systems is given and the circuitry diagrammed. (from paper)

entry.dc:title: Area strip mine reclamation using dredged material: a field demonstration.
entry.dc:creator: Perrier E.
entry.dc:description: This report describes the application of dredged material for area strip mine reclamation as a possible alternative to the present practices of dredged material disposal. The purpose of the study was to demonstrate the feasibility of using a cover of dewatered dredged material to reclaim surface mine spoils. The goal of reclamation effort was the prevention and abatement of erosion and acid mine drainage by the use of dredged material as a media for a vegetative cover. Chemical analysis of heavy metal uptake by tall fescue showed that the dredged material provided a suitable noncontaminating growth media. In addition, vegetation did not grow on the mine spoil control plot, but on the dredged material plots vegetation was produced that was both environmentally beneficial and aesthetically pleasing. (from authors' abstract)

entry.dc:description: Describes a study designed to compare erosion and gully development on seeded and unseeded sections of a mine dump complex. Rates of retreat and gully form are quite different on the two slopes. -Keith Clayton

entry.dc:title: A drainage model for a reclaimed surface mine.
entry.dc:creator: Prunty L.
entry.prism:publicationName: Soil Science Society of America Journal
entry.dc:description: Stripmine reclamation for row-crop production employing bench-terraced geometry is under study and may become increasingly common. A simplified model of the postreclamation soil profile at the Iowa Coal Project Demonstration Mine No. 1 is created. The model is used to find the steady-state water-table shape if one drain per terrace is installed. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: CRUSHED STONE PROVES TO BE A PROFITABLE PRODUCT IN A SURFACE COAL MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Robertson J.L.
entry.dc:description: Faster access to a valuable coal seam is the result of the use of a custom-designed drill at the Waterloo Coal Co. , Oak Hill, Ohio. The drill, a twin-boom hydraulic jumbo, penetrates the 7-ft-thick limestone seam that overlies the coal in approximately one-third the time required by the pneumatic drill previously used. As a secondary benefit, removal of the limestone provides a profitable product which, when processed and sold, helps reduce the costs of extracting the coal from the surface mine. The rock product plant and its components and operations are described. Land reclamation aspects are considered briefly.

entry.dc:title: Landsat remote sensing: observations of an Appalachian mountain- top surface coal mining and reclamation operation ( Kentucky).
entry.dc:description: The poential benefits of using Landsat remote sensing data by state agencies as an aide in monitoring surface coal mining operations are reviewed. A mountaintop surface mine in eastern Kentucky was surveyed over a 5 yr period using satellite multispectral scanner data that were classified by computer analyses. -from NASA Abstract E82-10247

entry.dc:title: Application of satellite data to surface mine monitoring in selected counties of South Carolina,.
entry.dc:creator: Bayne J.
entry.dc:description: Landsat data were used to explore the capability of digital imagery to monitor mining and reclamation activity in several S Carolina mining operations. Differentiation between active spoil partially and completely reclaimed areas was successfully demonstrated including small mining operations of less than 30 acres.-from STAR, 18(17), 1980
